Exact claim from survey: Reward hacking is commonly used for behavior in which optimizing an imperfect proxy degrades performance against the intended objective; formal analyses call the corresponding proxy-policy relation reward gaming.
A poor answer is not by itself reward hacking: evidence of an exploitable proxy and behavior that benefits from the mismatch is needed.
Expected supporting evidence: Formal definition and application to operational boundary

Exact claim from survey: Deshpande et al.'s TRACE benchmark frames detection as contrastive anomaly identification among coding trajectories and reports that contextualized, semantically expressed exploits are harder to identify than syntactic ones.
Expected supporting evidence: Benchmark task setup and contextualization results

Exact claim from survey: Baker et al. demonstrate monitoring of coding-agent traces and report that CoT can expose behavior not evident from actions alone.
Expected supporting evidence: Experiment comparing CoT and action/output monitoring

Exact claim from survey: When monitor scores are used in training, stronger optimization can induce obfuscation while hacking persists.
Expected supporting evidence: Training optimization results and obfuscation examples

Exact claim from survey: Wang et al.'s TRACE repeatedly truncates reasoning and checks whether the answer already earns reward; unusually early success is evidence for a shortcut, including cases with benign-looking traces.
Wilhelm et al. train sparse autoencoders and token-level classifiers over residual-stream activations to monitor during generation.
Expected supporting evidence: Method details for SAE features and tokenwise estimates

Exact claim from survey: Bergen et al. use difference-of-means activation vectors as inexpensive probes and report online prediction of later hacks in evaluated models.
Expected supporting evidence: Probe construction and temporal prediction evaluation

Exact claim from survey: Huang et al. show that LLM review of submitted code and scores misses some confirmed evaluation exploits in autonomous research tasks.
Expected supporting evidence: Confirmed-hack set and review-panel false-negative analysis
